name: IRF4905PBF
title: -55 V, -74 A P-channel HEXFET power MOSFET in TO-220
summary: A single P-channel power MOSFET in a three-lead through-hole TO-220 package, rated -55 V drain to source with 0.02 Ω maximum on-resistance at -10 V gate drive. It carries -74 A continuously with the case at 25 °C and dissipates up to 200 W there; the junction may run from -55 °C to 175 °C. It is avalanche rated (930 mJ single pulse) and lead-free.

circuits.title: Fig 10a. Switching Time Test Circuit
circuits.description: Resistive-load switching test. A -10 V gate pulse, at most 1 µs long and repeated at no more than 0.1 % duty, drives the gate through RG while RD loads the drain from a negative VDD. Watching VGS and VDS together gives the delay, rise and fall times: each is read between the 10 % and 90 % levels of the two waveforms (Fig 10b).

circuits.title: Fig. 12a. Unclamped Inductive Test Circuit
circuits.description: Avalanche test. A separate driver transistor, switched by a 15 V pulse, closes the loop from VDD through a 0.01 Ω current shunt, the device under test and inductor L. The DUT's gate gets a -20 V pulse of width tp through RG; current builds in L to IAS, and when the DUT turns off its drain is driven into breakdown, V(BR)DSS, until the inductor's current has fallen to zero (Fig 12b). The diode from the inductor's far end returns to the driver side of the shunt.

circuits.title: Fig 13b. Gate Charge Test Circuit
circuits.description: Gate charge measurement. A -3 mA current pulse charges the gate of the device under test while a current regulator, a second part of the same type held at a fixed gate bias, sets the drain current from the VDS supply. The bias comes from a 12 V cell across a 50 kΩ potentiometer, decoupled by 0.2 µF and 0.3 µF. Two sampling resistors in the return measure the gate and drain currents. The gate voltage against charge gives Qgs, the plateau charge Qgd, and the total QG to -10 V (Fig 13a).

circuits.title: Fig 14. Peak Diode Recovery dv/dt Test Circuit for P-Channel HEXFET Power MOSFETs
circuits.description: Body-diode recovery test. The DUT has its gate shorted to its source, so only its body diode conducts. A driver transistor, pulsed through RG, builds current in an inductor fed from VDD through a sense resistor; when the driver turns off, that current freewheels through the DUT's body diode, and when it turns on again the diode recovers and VDD is re-applied across the DUT. RG sets the recovery dv/dt and the drive's duty factor D sets ISD. A current transformer with a resistor across its secondary reads the diode current. Polarities are reversed for a P-channel DUT.

equations.name: Duty factor of the dv/dt test

operation.text: Every voltage and current at the drain and gate is negative in normal use: the gate goes below the source to switch on. The guaranteed on-resistance is 0.02 Ω at VGS = -10 V. The channel begins to conduct between -2.0 V and -4.0 V of gate drive.

With -44 V and -38 A at the drain, taking the gate to -10 V needs at most 180 nC, of which 32 nC is gate-to-source and 86 nC gate-to-drain charge. In Fig 6 the gate voltage rises to a plateau near -5 V, stays there while the drain swings, then climbs again.

The -74 A and 200 W ratings hold with the case at 25 °C; power falls by 1.3 W for each °C above that, and continuous current is -52 A at a 100 °C case (Fig 9 shows the full derating, reaching zero at 175 °C). Junction to case is 0.75 °C/W max, case to a flat greased heatsink 0.50 °C/W typical, and junction to free air 62 °C/W max. On-resistance rises with temperature, to about 1.8 times its 25 °C value at 175 °C (Fig 4).

A single avalanche pulse may carry 930 mJ, starting from TJ = 25 °C with 1.3 mH, RG = 25 Ω and IAS = -38 A. Repeated avalanche is limited to -38 A and 20 mJ per pulse, with the junction kept within its maximum. Fig 12c gives the allowed single-pulse energy against starting temperature for -16 A, -27 A and -38 A.

The source-to-drain diode carries -74 A continuous and -260 A pulsed. It drops at most -1.6 V at -38 A with the gate off. Recovering from -38 A at 100 A/µs takes 89 ns typical, 130 ns max, and 230 nC typical, 350 nC max. The drain may rise at up to -5.0 V/ns during recovery for ISD ≤ -38 A and di/dt ≤ -270 A/µs.

In the switching test, td(on) runs from 10 % of the gate pulse to 10 % of the drain change, tr from there to 90 %; td(off) and tf are taken the same way on the trailing edge (Fig 10b, Switching Time Waveforms; its caption misprints it as Fig 10a).

The dv/dt rating is tested with the device's body diode freewheeling an inductor that a second, pulsed transistor charges from VDD; the DUT's gate is tied to its source and its current is watched through a low-leakage current transformer. RG on the driving switch sets dv/dt, and the drive's duty factor sets ISD. The test layout keeps stray inductance low over a ground plane. For a P-channel DUT the circuit is used with the device's polarity reversed. The waveforms show the drive at VGS = 10 V (5.0 V for logic-level and 3 V drive parts), the diode current with its reverse-recovery dip, the re-applied VDD with the recovery dv/dt, and the inductor current with ripple of 5 % or less.
The package fixes with a 6-32 or M3 screw at up to 10 lbf·in (1.1 N·m). Leads may be soldered at 300 °C for 10 s, 1.6 mm from the case. The TO-220 is not recommended for surface mounting.

The top face carries the part number, the logo, a date code and the assembly lot code. The date code is a year digit (0 = 2000), a two-digit week and an assembly line letter; a 'P' in the line position marks a lead-free part.
